defects.description: ParseCents multiplies a binary float by 100 and truncates the result to an integer, so an amount that is not representable in binary loses a cent: "1.15" becomes 114, although the README promises the exact value in cents.
defects.why_missed: The suite parses amounts whose hundredths happen to be exactly representable (45.00, 0.05) and then round-trips them with FormatCents, so the truncation never changes a value the tests look at.

defects.description: Split gives every share the truncated quotient and never hands out the remainder, so splitting a total that does not divide evenly loses cents: Split(1000, 3) returns shares that add up to 999 although the README promises their sum is the total.
defects.why_missed: The only split test divides 1000 by 4, where the quotient is exact and the missing remainder is zero, so the invariant the README states is never checked against a total with a remainder.
